column2: Sheriffs reportedly showed a construction crew one suspect photo on Wednesday; the image the FBI released Thursday reportedly did not look like it. An electrician described a man in a black trench coat, mask and long greasy hair.

Stairwell photos went out at a 7:58 PM press conference; court documents reportedly put the Miranda warning at 6:25 PM the same evening. The Director described the images as "enhanced" and nobody has said on the record what that meant.
The "Valhalla" remark, the repeated "33 hours," and a roof clip one commentator compared to 1973 VHS. Counted from the shot, 33 hours lands hours after the reported 6:25 PM Miranda time.

The hub for every federal thread — the briefings, the ballistics, the halted foreign-nexus inquiry, and the witness who says he was advised to erase his own video. Start here if this is your first FBI page.
A .30-06 carries roughly 3,950 joules, about eight times a 9mm. The arithmetic is not in dispute; what commentators dispute is whether the wound described publicly can be squared with it.

A rooftop rifle shooter should leave gunshot residue. Citizen compilations allege the standard GSR test was never run, while DNA on the recovered rifle is described as a complex mixture rather than one profile.
Roughly 600,000 files were reportedly produced while the raw DNA data, ballistics scans and chain-of-custody logs stayed contested. Critics frame it as volume used to obscure rather than to disclose.

Two commenters identifying themselves as a surgeon and a retired cardiologist read the Medical Examiner findings and said the same thing from different specialties — the injury list does not fit one downward rifle round. Their credentials are unverified.

The reported claim is that bomb-sniffing dogs were kept from certain zones of the scene. If a device was involved, K-9 screening was the one method most likely to have caught it — days before the ground was paved.

Low-resolution roof video was released while higher-fidelity campus archives reportedly stayed in. The same page tracks the reported requests that witnesses delete their own phone video and the disposal of the transport SUV.
Four claims the public was given — a confession, the father's identification, suicidal ideation, a lone gunman — set beside what the record actually shows. Each is contested; none is settled.

The ATF reportedly found the jacket fragment shared class characteristics with the Mauser — numerous makes and models, no individual match. The defense was then reportedly refused permission to photograph it or attend the destructive testing.

Police dispatch, a construction crew, and the only pre-shooting roof video independently described a man in all black with long greasy hair. That silhouette does not match the T-shirt and jeans of the charged man.

Several on-camera witnesses described a chest or heart wound within minutes of the shot. None has been called to testify in the case built on the state's rifle theory, so the accounts survive only as interviews.

Every camera sighting the released timeline attributes to the charged man on September 10 and 11, hour by hour. Cameras record movement, not names — which is exactly the gap the identity dispute lives in.

An electrician says a man in all black told the crew someone had been shot. The page rates its own evidence and states plainly that panic-moment eyewitness descriptions are among the weakest evidence there is.
Mike Glover says a senior CIA contact told him agency personnel were turned around at the airport and blocked from the case. He says the interference was reported up the chain and nothing was done.

The working memo on federal posture — sealed forensics, the field-office leadership change, aviation telemetry, finance questions, and witness coordination, each written as a lead to corroborate or refute. Start here before drilling into any single FBI thread.

One hypothesis, six anomalies: the dogs, the paving, the necklace, the absent footage, the skipped GSR test. The page gives the innocent reading of every item equal space and says outright that convergence is not proof.

Post-blast residue is not fragile trace evidence that vanishes in an afternoon. It transfers readily, lodges in synthetic fibre, and comes back out under solvent extraction — which makes clothing and soil testable objects, not lost ones.

Before the hardscape crew ever arrived, roughly ten inches of soil was already gone — dug out by a different, still-unidentified crew described in the record only as men working for the state of Utah.
PETN is destructive far out of proportion to its size and can be molded into thin sheets or slivers. Reporting on the 2024 pager operation is why capability arguments keep circling back to it.

One page for what the majority of citizen investigators concluded actually killed Charlie Kirk, and what did not. The official account is a single .30-06 round; most independent investigators working the case do not accept it.

Why would an eastern FBI office surface in a Utah homicide? The record notes a reported ADL co-location in the same Connecticut building and asks for the travel orders and the case-file assignment that would settle it.

Joe Kent, then NCTC director, says the FBI shut his inquiry down before he could run out his leads. The Bureau publicly said foreign intelligence was assisting — assistance and shutdown, at the same time, on the same threads.
The field office with jurisdiction over UVU changed hands about a month before September 10, and the incoming SAC fronted the first press conference. A judge on the case was sworn in the same week.

Claims and questions about CIA involvement, including a campus national-security society whose online profiles reportedly came down two weeks after the shooting. Every listing is unverified and nobody on it is accused of anything.

A counterterrorism review of possible foreign involvement reportedly escalated to a tense White House meeting and was told to stop. Reported allegation from public statements and interviews, not a court finding.

Joe Kent, in his own words on a July 2026 podcast, describing how the NCTC's parallel review of foreign ties was halted early. Attributable and on the record — which is why investigators weight it above anonymous posts.
A pointer page that keeps the federal intelligence thread from being mistaken for campus police or sheriff work. It still bears on the state timeline, which is why the local reader is sent to it.

The contractor says he was told "the governor and the FBI said they want this by Monday" and laid pavers four days after the killing. Doing pavers correctly means over-excavating — stripping the exact soil layer residue clings to.

Court restrictions, closed hearings, and reported hospital NDAs, while the Charlie Kirk Show reportedly faced no equivalent limit. The judge who entered the order was sworn in weeks before September 10.

Candace Owens reports being told the FBI took the security detail's clothing down to their underwear — which would explain the hospital scrubs. Bagging boxer briefs is textbook evidence collection; releasing the transport vehicle is not.

If Israel is treated as a suspect, why is Israeli-made software extracting and authenticating the trial evidence? The striking part of the answer is that the defense has the data and is not raising it.

Alleged Israeli and Washington IP search spikes on the campus layout, the hospital, the judges and defense counsel — weeks or months before September 10. Unverified; log-level records would settle it in one line.

The Israeli digital-forensics firm whose extraction tools were described in courtroom testimony as having been used on a phone in the case. Widely used commercial software; the page alleges no wrongdoing by anyone.
Search-interest records for rooftop, parking and CCTV queries reportedly disappeared after the event. Researchers archive Trends screenshots precisely because live results shift under them.

Sealed warrants, withheld DNA mixture data, and a reported 600,000-file production. The defense reportedly asked to photograph the bullet fragment and watch the testing, and was told policy does not allow it.

Interior hospital cameras were reportedly seized while the manhunt was still running outside. Those cameras are the only record of who entered treatment areas, and whether the emergency room was cleared and on whose authority.
"As per SBI and FBI, we've been given clear direction NOT to interview." One witness says he sent in close-up 4K footage to help, then got calls asking him to confirm he had deleted it.

The contractor's own first-person account of the call, the emergency order, and the Sunday install. His crew was the second phase — by his account the ground had already been dug out before he arrived.
The video that put the pave-over into the public record, with a full transcription of what the contractor says on camera. Roughly 93,000 views at the time it was captured.
Sealing the pad is a separate act from hauling the soil away — different crew phase, different surface, different records to request. Work orders and invoices, not dump manifests.

Medical forensics does not stop at the body. If the tent ground was hardscaped within days, wound-origin reconstruction and trace recovery both get harder, and the page names the entities cited online.

A page of the actual defense filing, arguing the State has not met its burden on reliable evidence and cannot establish the high-probability-of-death aggravator. Read the document rather than the summary of it.

The defense asked to photograph the bullet fragment and attend future testing, and was refused. The page separates the real January motion from the planted-evidence framing that got attached to it online.
The public record on the charges and evidence handling, plus the sealing questions commentators raise. Digital-forensics warrants were reportedly sealed well into 2026, limiting outside review.

A September 2025 ATF laboratory report summarized in court filings calls the link inconclusive. On the state's own science, the recovered rifle cannot be forensically proven to have fired the autopsy fragment.
If the rights warning came at 6:25 PM and the phone went into evidence, who typed the Discord messages at 7:57? A single login-IP record that nobody has published would settle it.
Backpack, hat, trousers and rifle-carry plausibility, compared side by side. An outfit change should shrink a pack, and the stairwell pack reads fuller — which is the whole argument.
Six mismatch points between the man on the morning campus cameras and the figure on the stairs. The page does not claim to know who the stairs figure is; it claims the two do not match.
Fifty hours of one official's public statements, each set against what the rest of the file shows was happening at that moment. A suspect was announced, then quietly un-announced.
The campus HD network is the backbone of the probable-cause affidavit, yet the public has reportedly only ever seen re-encoded press clips — never the original DVR exports.
A witness says he sent close-up 4K/60 footage to the Bureau to help, and was then called repeatedly to confirm he had deleted his copy. He says he kept it anyway.

A Bombardier Global 6500 flown by an Army ISR contractor, publicly tied to the HADES program, that flew a low, slow profile near the campus corridor on September 10. No track or tasking order has surfaced in the prosecution.
The institutional camera system the affidavit stitches into a suspect track from 11:50 to 12:23. What it never captured is any imagery settling how Charlie Kirk was killed.

Every reported cover-up allegation, grouped by the kind of cover-up alleged — scene alteration, kill mechanism, foreign leads, witnesses, records. Reported allegations the site tracks, not findings it asserts.

The caption, the docket, the charges, and what the state actually alleges — separated from what has been proven. The defense disputes the forensic links, starting with the inconclusive ATF comparison.

One actor followed from the August 2025 field-office change through the September announcements, the halted parallel inquiries, and the records fights that followed. Timestamps and public statements, not conclusions.

The domestic agencies — CIA, NSA, ODNI and NCTC, and defense intelligence — examined for what they collected and what they declined to pursue. The counterpart hub for non-U.S. services sits elsewhere on the site.
Reported allegations that a counterterrorism review of a possible foreign role was shut down before its leads were run out. Every official named is a living public figure presumed innocent.
The leads pointing outside the United States — phones, travel, SIGINT, search patterns — and the prior question of whether the government ran any of them down at all.

An Egyptian-registered Falcon 7X reportedly on the ground near Provo from September 4, departing in the hours around the assassination. The claims come from open-source ADS-B researchers, and the innocent readings are laid out too.
The center that integrates terrorism intelligence across agencies, its chain of command running up to the President, and the reported order that stopped its foreign-involvement inquiry.

A gag order entered on the court's own motion, closed preliminary sessions, and sealed filings around the inconclusive ballistics report. Fair-trial advocates defend every one of those steps in a capital case.
Lawful censorship still shapes what the public can hear. The order was reportedly entered without either side asking for it, and the research file flags a podcast-shaped gap in its reach.
Media barred, no transcripts issued, later sessions ordered closed as well. The page rates the claim EMERGING and says outright that closing a session is lawful and is not sealing a record forever.

Charlie Kirk was taken to a Level IV hospital about 2.6 miles away rather than the Level II trauma centre run by a different health system. Standard protocol favours the highest-level capability available.

A rare page that turns on its own source: the investigation file contradicts itself three lines apart and retracts one of its own claims inside the same paragraph. Those failures are stated plainly instead of repeated.
The ten minutes from the shot to the hospital doors, second by second, where nearly every enduring dispute in this case is seeded. Every source in the window disagrees with the others.

Footage never released, an emergency room that reportedly looked unusually empty, and staff at a nearby facility reportedly asked to sign non-disclosure agreements. Presented as questions, not conclusions.

The police-side booking document that established the legal basis for the detention — and the first place the government commits to its theory of how Charlie Kirk was killed. The full PDF is on the page.
Official Bureau channels are the citation layer under every wire-service sentence. When that layer wobbles — a premature custody announcement, for instance — the whole media stack wobbles with it.
Four documents describe the same arrest and they do not agree on when it happened. The booking sheet says 10:00 PM on the 11th; the police system record says 04:00 on the 12th.

Two official records reportedly give arrest times six hours apart, and the earlier one predates the affidavit's own arrival time. The page notes that one custody event routinely generates several timestamps.
The majority citizen finding, set out in full: a small concealed device rather than a round from a distant rifle. The page asks you to read the skeptic counterargument before sharing any clip.

The first person taken into custody shouted words to the effect of "I shot him, now shoot me," and later told police he said it to draw attention from the real shooter. He was cleared as the shooter the same day.

The alleged text confession says the outfit was changed in the woods. An electrician working above those woods described the man who walked up to him — and the two descriptions are not the same person.

The competing theories of who killed Charlie Kirk, laid out side by side rather than merged: foreign service, domestic agency, the charged man, patsies and distraction actors. Contested readings of the public record, not court findings.

The hub for the exploding-mic case — the RODE lavalier, the high-explosive chemistry, the frame analysis, the audio, and the residue that would settle it. Start with the investigation index and follow whichever question brought you.

The most-repeated suspicion about how Charlie Kirk died: no exit wound, no spray, from a round carrying roughly 2,900 foot-pounds. The page also gives the ordinary pathology baseline that cuts against it.
A 5 to 9 degree downward shot from the rooftop should enter the face or jaw first. The reported entry sits between larynx and trachea, reading far more straight-on than steep.
Arm-to-arm search: nothing. K-9 pass: nothing. Then federal agents reportedly told three junior local officers to search the area again, and the rifle appeared.

In the weeks before September 10 the court, the Salt Lake FBI field office and the treating hospital each changed leadership. Timing alone proves nothing, which is why the page is a timeline and an open question.
The judge presiding over the case, sworn in on August 4, 2025 — reportedly the same period the Salt Lake field office changed hands. The case is described in commentary as his first on the bench.
Google Trends shows aggregate, anonymized interest and identifies nobody. The page says so up front, then records the spikes citizen researchers keep pointing at anyway.

A new hospital chief executive started roughly two weeks before September 10 — on its face routine. The page also kills a viral claim outright: he is an administrator, not a surgeon, and did not treat anyone.

The clothing worn by the people closest to Kirk in the minutes after the shot is exactly the substrate residue testing works on. Whether it was ever tested is the question; the claim itself is secondhand and unverified.

The vehicle that carried Charlie Kirk to the hospital is, to skeptics, a primary forensic surface. Commentary alleges it was scrapped and disposed of before any independent testing — reported, not confirmed.
Described in the file as head of security and one of five people in the SUV, reportedly shielding Kirk with his own body. Attributed claims about a role, with no assertion of foreknowledge or intent.

No ambulance, no sirens — carried into a private vehicle by his own detail. Using the car already on hand in a chaotic scene is not evidence of wrongdoing, which is why the page is about who controlled the evidence, not about rescue.

The allegation is that local police were directed not to interview witnesses and were separately tied up elsewhere, so the on-scene record was thinned at the source. Radio traffic and eyewitness accounts are what it rests on.
Attendee accounts of phone clips that were missing or looked edited by the time they got home. Anecdotal, unverified, and collected because the same pattern keeps recurring across separate witnesses.

Firsthand accounts from people who were there, indexed by what they saw, heard, and from which direction. Almost none of it appears in the prosecution — which is precisely why it is gathered and preserved here.

A named witness describing his own experience, which the page rates above an anonymous claim. It also states the ordinary reading: asking a witness not to keep graphic footage is common and lawful once the original is secured.

Structure, leadership, security arrangements, donors and internal dynamics — summarized so a reader can see why the organization keeps appearing in the investigation. It is not a claim that the organization is responsible for anything.
The firm reportedly providing private security on the day, and the vendor switch that preceded it. Several names circulating online as on-site staff are unverified photo matches, not roster entries.
A former representative's public allegation, presented as a reported claim and nothing more. The page asks only that the testimony be properly investigated so the truth can come out.
The non-U.S. services hub: foreign phones at the venue, Egyptian air-force tail numbers, search-pattern claims, and the blocked follow-up. Presence, motive and obstruction — not a courtroom finding.

Hezbollah reportedly switched to pagers to escape smartphone tracking, and that switch was allegedly anticipated. The page sits here as a capability reference only — no tampered device has been alleged in Charlie Kirk's death.

Background on the target of the September 2024 pager operation, carried so the comparison can be judged on facts rather than on an unfamiliar foreign event. Nothing links Hezbollah or Lebanon to the Kirk case.

Four of the alleged sixteen UVU devices reportedly pinged a hotel hosting US–Iran talks in April 2026. The poster labelled his own tracking graphic a recreation, which is where the claim starts and stops.
The working memo for this whole section, sorted into a motive layer, an execution-adjacent layer and a response layer. Read it first if you want the map before the individual claims.
What has been claimed about Israeli people, devices and institutions near this case, and on what kind of public evidence. The page is as careful with the benign explanations as with the allegations.
Capability context and nothing more: what the service is, why commentators name it, and why being able to do something is not evidence of having done it.

A former Turning Point representative's on-camera account of what he says he was asked during training. Single-source and uncorroborated — published so it can be investigated, not because it has been established.
The alleged twelve to sixteen Israeli-registered phones at UVU, plus the wider forty-four foreign-device breakdown. No NSA, DOJ or FBI document confirming any of it has been released publicly.

Thousands of pagers detonating across two countries in two days, and the argument commentators build on top of it. The 2024 event is documented; its application to Charlie Kirk is an argument about capability.

Brand says two people who were in a cabinet meeting told him foreign involvement and domestic accomplices were both taken off the table six days in. Anonymous second-hand sourcing, unconfirmed by anyone named.
Carroll's seven-minute case that a foreign-motive question deserves asking, delivered with his own caveat that it does not mean Israel did it. Attributed opinion, printed with its counterpoint.
The contested claim of Israeli presence on campus on September 10, split into SIGINT, sightings and search patterns. Presence near an event does not establish participation in it.
The reported motive narratives in one place: shifting rhetoric, donor pressure, and what friends say changed through 2025. Motive is not proof, and the page says so before it says anything else.
An archival clip in which Western politicians who block an Iran war are told they "will fall." Asked directly what he meant, the speaker answered elections — the part most reposts leave out.

A living private citizen whose reported account of the Bridgehampton weekend shifted between an X post and later sworn questioning. His own published text denies that Charlie Kirk was bullied or threatened.

The one document that should say plainly how he died is a restricted record in Utah for roughly fifty years. Commentary says a hospital physician signed it rather than the medical examiner — while sworn testimony says the state office did conduct an autopsy.

Seven surgeons at the receiving hospital were reportedly searched from Israeli IP addresses across two weeks in July 2025. The page also corrects the widely shared claim that the hospital's new chief executive was the treating surgeon — he is an administrator, not a physician.

The viral claim kept in one place so it can be tested rather than repeated: no autopsy, a death certificate signed by a hospital doctor, a body moved fast. An ATF filing describing fragments recovered during the autopsy cuts against the strongest version of it.
The autopsy subsection: whether one happened, who signed what, and why nine pages the court has already seen are still not public. Start here before judging any single wound claim.

Every competing account of the wound argued side by side — entry versus exit, the rifle round, a device at the microphone, decorticate posturing. With no published report the argument runs on video and physics rather than pathology.

Thirty-three to fifty minutes from the shot to the pronouncement, reconstructed from video, transport estimates and operating-room notes. The page also flags a foreign newspaper reportedly announcing the death before that window had closed.

Arrival, interventions, time of death — none of it released, and none of it aired in the court case. What remains is a receiving facility, a chief executive two weeks into the job, and questions nobody has answered on the record.

Trained medics reportedly asking to be let in, an emergency room described as strangely empty, and non-disclosure agreements nobody has produced. Each claim is set beside the ordinary explanation that also fits it.
Why the farther, lower-level hospital, what happened inside it, and where the records went afterwards. The whole hospital cluster in one place, with the protocol context that may explain all of it.

The working memo for the entire medical thread: five priority questions first, then every page routed under autopsy, hospital, wounds and people. It closes with the specific records that would settle the argument.

Rooftop rifle, close-range pistol, or a charge worn on the body — the mechanism arguments laid out against the reported entry between larynx and trachea. A rooftop round on a five-to-nine degree downward path should have met the jaw first.

If a busload of emergency-room patients really left the hospital ninety minutes before the shot, somebody booked it, somebody drove it, and somebody signed for it at the other end. This page is about that paper trail, which nobody has produced.

Office leadership and the hands-on pathologist are two different names, and the case keeps merging them. Sworn testimony named Dr. Guajardo as the doctor who performed the examination; the chief examiner most people name is someone else entirely.

Nine pages, admitted as State's Exhibit 11, read aloud by a witness who did not write them and never published. Two lines from page one are all the public firmly has: homicide, and a gunshot wound of the neck.

The sharpest version of the hospital tip: a chart for Charlie Kirk reportedly sitting in the system of a hospital he was never taken to, before the shot. The page pulls the two stacked oddities apart, because they fail or survive separately.
Months on, no doctor or nurse who treated him has been publicly named. The page separates that transparency gap from the false claim that the hospital's chief executive performed the surgery.

The vehicle reportedly met at the surgery doors rather than the emergency entrance, twenty to thirty minutes in an operating room, then a second SUV in physician parking. Reported eyewitness accounts, recorded with the caveats they need.

"The bullet did not exit" is one of the most repeated medical claims in the case, and it reaches the public only second-hand through affiliated relays. No named physician has ever said it on the record.

A hospital that size runs cameras, and not one frame from September 10 has been released. The page is careful about what it is: an open question and a demand for footage, not a finding that anything was removed.

A chief medical examiner ten weeks into the job, a hospital chief executive sixteen days into his, and two reported departures afterwards. Turnover is ordinary — the page asks only whether this much of it inside one window is.

A woman who says she used to work at the hospital argues the destination was the strange part, not the distance: the Level II centre was about a mile farther. She was not there that day, and she is not named.

Mechanism of injury either supports the state's account or dismantles it, and the report that would answer it is not public. This hub organises every reported fact, expert reading and labelled claim underneath that one question.

Charts moving between two hospitals owned by different companies leave an interface log or a signed packet behind. That is the useful part of this claim: either the audit trail exists for that morning or it does not.

Emergency-room patients were reportedly told at about 11:30 AM that they were being shuttled to another hospital — roughly an hour before the shot. The page keeps the appeal for witnesses separate from a conclusion nobody has earned yet.

The first step of the tip, isolated: staff reportedly moving everyone out of the emergency room into another wing during the ten o'clock hour. That is more than two hours before any hospital could have been reacting to a shooting.

A surgeon — explicitly not Charlie Kirk's — was reportedly warned that if he came in for his September 10 operation he would not be leaving for a long time. Everything turns on what time that call was made, and nobody knows.

A hospital does not receive 911 calls, which is why this secondhand tip needs care before it becomes evidence. Read as no ambulance pre-alert reaching the emergency room, it is exactly what a security-driven private transport would produce.

The umbrella page for the whole clear-out account: wing move, shuttles, files, and a chart that should not have existed yet. One anonymous tip, four separable claims, and the records that would settle each one.

One bullet jacket fragment and four lead fragments came out of the autopsy, and the state's own lab could not tie them to the seized rifle. The FBI then planned a destructive re-examination the defense was reportedly refused permission to watch or record.

Utah criminalised sharing medical-examiner autopsy photographs and videos four months before September 10, on the earliest default date a bill can take. The page gives the ordinary legislative explanation alongside the timing question rather than choosing between them.

What Utah law and ordinary medical-examiner practice actually require in a violent death, set against what the public has been given. Context first, so the arguments about a missing report can be judged rather than repeated.

The working memo for the whole section: five priority questions first, then every argument routed under forensics, identity, timeline and mechanism. It closes with the disclosure targets that would settle each one.

Witnesses near the tent mostly described pops, fireworks or a pistol — not the heavy crack of a rifle fired 120 metres away. The page also records a campus alert declaring a suspect in custody nineteen minutes in, when nobody was.

One bystander angle catches a figure in head-to-toe black reaching the open rear hatch of the vehicle used to move Charlie away from the courtyard. The camera pans off within a second. The identity is unknown and no wrongdoing is alleged.

A worker on the site above the courtyard reportedly spoke to a man coming up from the shooting who asked to cut through — before any siren sounded. The same video records the evidence trail sitting unsecured while the public walked through it.

The complete transcript of the 11:47 escape-path investigation, so the broadcast clips and witness quotes can be searched and quoted directly rather than through a summary. It opens with an accuracy note listing the machine-transcription errors that matter.

The working memo for every alternative-suspect thread, organised by question rather than by page. Dispatch description, van hatch, laser reflection, shooter positions — each paired with the record that would close it.

Social-media allegations placing a named private citizen at the rear of the grey van, recorded here as tips and FOIA framing rather than as findings. No agency has named him and no criminal allegation is made.

What the case looks like if Tyler Robinson is not the answer: a dispatch description of a man in black, a van under the tent tunnel, construction witnesses, and competing shooter positions. Persons of interest only — nobody here is accused.
